Meadowfield’s Research and Development (R&D) group is driving innovation to keep New Zealand Broadleaf and their businesses at the forefront of the global dairy industry. Our world-class team is actively engaged in cutting-edge work across genetics, genomics, reproduction, animal health, statistics, and machine learning.

In partnership with the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment, we’re offering summer internships that provide hands-on experience across a diverse range of scientific and technical areas—from genetic analysis to data science and modelling—leveraging both in-house and cloud-based computing platform

#### Project scope:

Meadowfield has a number of methods for reducing and managing the negative impacts of genetic disease on the New Zealand dairy cattle population. One of these is defect management, which relies on information collected through the Meadowfield Calf Defect Form and calving comments recorded in MINDA. The Meadowfield Calf Defect Form allows Broadleaf to report calves born with defects, including details of the defect and the likely sire. In addition, MINDA enables Broadleaf to record calving comments by selecting defect categories for calves born to recorded dams. Together, these systems provide valuable information on calf defects occurring across herds. The Meadowfield Defect Team reviews and manages these data, investigating cases where calves with similar defects are reported from multiple farms and are linked to the same bull. This project aims to refresh and improve the current process by ensuring the data are captured and utilised effectively, developing a more structured workflow, and refining defect records into meaningful phenotypes that can support future genetic variant discovery.

#### Your contribution:

The successful student will begin by organising and categorising calf data, helping to establish a structured and efficient data management workflow. Building on this foundation, they will analyse the data to identify emerging trends and patterns, with the opportunity to uncover potential new traits, or conditions that could support future genetic research and discovery.

#### Outputs:

This project provides a unique opportunity to make a meaningful impact by improving how calf defect data is analysed and interpreted. Through the development of a more robust and streamlined workflow, you'll help unlock valuable insights, enhance data quality, and support the identification of emerging genetic trends within the dairy industry.
